reciprocal.why: A cross-tradition pairing: wu wei's unforced action in which the world does most of the work, and Heidegger's release from willing.
Both are Heidegger's terms: letting-be from the technology essay, Gelassenheit from the Discourse on Thinking.
Both release the grip on what one clutches: Buddhist non-attachment on outcomes and possessions, Eckhart's letting-go on the 'mine-ness' of one's actions.
The SEP calls Eckhart's negative virtues Stoic-sounding, which is why the compendium pairs them with the Stoic freedom from passion.
The beginner's mind is empty of the expert's habits and open to possibilities; Heidegger's waiting expects nothing and holds no object.
Acceptance embraces unwanted experience without the struggle to change it; Gelassenheit is a release of willing. The compendium treats them as neighbours, not the same thing.
Dogen's just sitting and Heidegger's 'nothing but wait' are paired by the compendium as contemplative neighbours.
